programme: The list does not converge on one module. It splits into at least five unrelated functional clusters: epithelial-identity/EMT restraint (MTA3 represses SNAI1 and works with GRHL2, which itself represses ZEB1 and maintains CDH1/CLDN3/CLDN4 junctional genes); heat-shock/proteostasis (HSF4 driving HSPB1, HSP90AA1, CRYAB, HIF1A); neuronal-gene silencing (REST, with its canonical neuronal target catalogue); nuclear-receptor/xenobiotic and steroid corepression (NR1I2/PXR, NCOR1, NR2C1, each with large CYP/steroid-receptor target sets); and endocrine/muscle lineage specification (NEUROG3 driving islet genes, SMARCD3 driving MYOG/SGCA). ZNF219 and ZNF135 have target sets too small and unannotated to place in any of these. No more than two or three factors converge on any single named process, so this is a set of independently recurring regulators, not a module.
role_in_a: Only the epithelial-restraint pair (MTA3, GRHL2) has a plausible role in endometrioid cancer: both normally suppress the EMT programme (SNAI1, ZEB1) that drives invasion in endometrial carcinoma, and MTA3 sits at percentile 0.8857 in the Open Targets record for this disease, consistent with a real (if unremarkable) tumor-suppressive role for that axis. None of the other clusters (heat-shock, REST, nuclear-receptor corepression, endocrine/muscle specification) has an Open Targets association or literature hit tying it to endometrioid cancer specifically.
role_in_b: No named cluster has a documented role in fibromyalgia. REST is the only factor with an Open Targets score in fibromyalgia (percentile 0.5378, unremarkable), and there is a general literature on REST loss and nociceptor hyperexcitability, but that is a property of REST alone, not of the wider list. MTA3 and GRHL2, the strongest and most coherent pair, have no fibromyalgia association at all and their epithelial-junction biology has no obvious counterpart in a blood-derived, non-epithelial disorder.
shared_axis: No shared mechanism can be proposed. The strongest candidate module (MTA3+GRHL2 epithelial/EMT restraint) is tissue-restricted to epithelium and has no known or plausible function in the blood compartment from which the fibromyalgia network was built; the remaining clusters (heat-shock, REST, nuclear-receptor corepression, endocrine/muscle specification) are each carried by only one or two factors and have no cross-disease evidence connecting them either.
reasoning: Twelve factors recurring across many patient-group comparisons is a real statistical signal, but it does not resolve into one nameable programme: the factors split across five unrelated functions, and the largest coherent sub-cluster (MTA3/GRHL2) is epithelial biology with no route into a blood-tissue disease. The record itself flags this — Open Targets links only MTA3 (to disease A) and REST (to disease B), and every retrieved paper is explicitly noted as off-topic or unjudgeable for this pair. Forcing a single story here would be the kind of overreach the exclusions are meant to guard against.
how_to_falsify: Take the MTA3/GRHL2 target module (SNAI1, CDH1, ZEB1, CLDN3/4) as the best-case candidate axis and test it directly: profile PBMC or whole-blood transcriptomes from an independent fibromyalgia cohort for coordinated expression of this module, and compare direction/magnitude to MTA3/GRHL2 target regulation in endometrioid tumor versus matched normal endometrium. If the module is not coordinately regulated in blood, or is regulated but in a direction/context unrelated to epithelial-junction biology, that confirms the two recurrences are independent, supporting the incoherent verdict.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) versus uterine endometrium (endometrioid cancer) — a non-epithelial versus epithelial compartment — which is the main reason an epithelial-identity module cannot be assumed portable between them. The recurrence counts are drawn from 48 patient-group comparisons over only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the same two source studies likely underlie most of the concordance. The single-view exclusions remove group-specific noise but do not certify that what remains is cross-tissue-relevant, and the tissue-generic exclusion removed several immune/stress hub factors (SPI1, STAT3, IRF1, TWIST1, CEBPD) that might otherwise have supplied a plausible blood-epithelium connector — their removal is why the remaining list looks disconnected, not evidence that no connector exists at all.
